# Leaderboard

TTS is the standard time-to-solution metric (Ronnow et al. 2014):
$\mathrm{TTS}_p = \bar{t} \cdot \log(1-p) / \log(1-P_s)$, the expected total
time, running independent restarts, needed to be $p$-confident of finding the
best-found energy at least once, where $\bar{t}$ is the mean per-run time and
$P_s$ is the empirical single-run success probability. This site uses
$p = 0.99$, the field's standard convention.

A seed marked with **†** has a provable ground state (see
[Instance Library](implementation/instances.qmd#verified-ground-states)):
its exact energy, computed independently of any solver run, is shown in the
Reference Energy column. When the best energy any submitted run found for
that instance does not match the reference energy, the Best Algorithm column
shows "—", since no algorithm can be credited with having solved it.
